summary: A narrator, temporarily left in charge of an office by Rhindquist, has Tony sort shredded papers and then wanders through the Company's personnel files on the office computer. He reads his own file, his mother's, family records, and Buddy's, discovers that a Security Manager had Buddy jailed because the Manager was engaged to Buddy's ex-girlfriend Carla, and uses the system to free Buddy and Carla, promote them, and demote the Security Manager to janitor. The section ends with a shouted phone call demanding McBride, which the narrator answers while filling in for him.
one_line: A young office worker, briefly in charge, misuses access to personnel files to free his friend Buddy and punish a jealous Security Manager.
key_facts: Rhindquist calls the narrator 'Sonny-boy' and tells him he is going to do just fine.
Tony is ordered to get the papers from the third floor, sort them, box them, and have them on Rhindquist's desk by lunch.
The narrator opens the personnel files on the office TV and reads his own file, which goes back to the Infirmary where he was born.
The narrator discovers that his mother had her tubes tied.
Buddy's file is spotless up to the spying incident.
The Security Manager who 'caught' Buddy was engaged to Carla last year, and Carla is Buddy's ex-girlfriend.
The narrator gets Buddy and Carla out of jail, gives them promotions, and has the Security Manager busted down to a janitor.
Tony returns at lunchtime with three big boxes of papers, sorted into memos, personal documents, and inter-departmental communications.
The narrator compares himself to the queen ant watching the drones.
The narrator promises his mother a big Christmas bonus.
When the phone rings, the narrator answers 'Jasper Whitehead, Special Vice-President.'
The caller shouts, 'Get me McBride, now!'
The narrator tells the caller that McBride is not available and that he is filling in for him.
